IncBot: :rotating_light: Canary alert triggered for canary-id=canary-8742. p99 latency > 3s for streaming endpoints, SLO breach detected (p95=480ms, p99=3.2s) — auto-escalating to P0.
Maya: saw the alert, joining. Can confirm spike on streaming chat and chunked responses.
Tom: I'm seeing a jump in tail latency correlated with the new model v9.3 encoder rollout. Metric spike window ~ 3612345600-3612345660.
Elaine: paging SRE oncall (Liam) now. @Liam you're oncall?
Liam: oncall here. Looking at dashboard. p50 stable, p95 creeping up to ~600ms, but p99 tail is the problem. Streaming stalls and partial responses observed.
Maya: logs show repeated `kv_cache_miss` and `grpc_stream_reset` in canary pods. Pushing logs excerpt:```[2026-03-12T14:22:34Z] pod/canary-8742-5 kvcache miss key=enc-uid-12, latency=12ms
[2026-03-12T14:22:35Z] pod/canary-8742-5 grpc: stream reset by peer, code=14
[2026-03-12T14:22:36Z] pod/canary-8742-5 response chunk delay=1.8s```
Kevin: interesting — could be model size + quant path causing occasional kernel fallbacks. Are canary pods autoscaled appropriately?
Tom: autoscaling looks fine; CPU/GPU utilization modest. This looks like dynamic memory thrash on KV caches leading to stalls.
Liam: mitigation plan proposals: 1) Immediately reduce canary traffic back to 0% (halt rollout). 2) Shift traffic to stable v9.2 model. 3) Enable fallback routing to smaller encoder variant for streaming requests. 4) Notify customers and CS.
Maya: agreed. I'm going to run the abort: `redwoodctl rollout abort --id canary-8742 --reason "p99 spike streaming stalls"`
Tom: I'll prepare a temporary routing rule to pin requests to stable: `trafficctl set-route --service=chat-stream --model=v9.2 --weight=100 --scope=prod`
Elaine: I'll create incident ticket and customer impact notes. Amy from CS looping in on possible affected accounts. @Amy can you assess customer-facing risk?
Amy: on it. Pulling list of customers who received requests in the 14:22-14:24 window. Immediate note: one mid-market customer reported multiple truncated responses to users in that timeframe (support ticket #CS-11290). Will prepare a C-level brief.
IncBot: Rollout abort command received: redwoodctl accepted abort for canary-8742 by Maya at 3612345682.
Maya: abort executed. Confirming canary pods terminating.
Liam: traffic shift in flight — monitoring. p99 dropped from 3.2s to 860ms within 30s of the abort, p95 back to ~420ms.
Tom: still seeing a small number of lingering stream resets from the canary nodes, but no new ones from stable. Logs:```[2026-03-12T14:23:10Z] pod/canary-8742-2 terminating, flush started
[2026-03-12T14:23:15Z] pod/stable-923 acks/resumed streams, latency=380ms```
Kevin: for postmortem, recommend: telemetry on kv cache eviction rates per model, memory pressure sampling, and kernel fallback counters exposed. Also add a quick toggle in the rollout pipeline to disable encoder-quant path for canaries.
Maya: agree — file followups. Creating a TODO in incident: - capture model-specific kv eviction metrics - add rollout guard that forces slower warmup traffic before wider rollout - add auto-rollback on repeated p99 > 2s within 5 minutes.
Elaine: CS notified customers in the affected window, drafted message: "We observed intermittent truncated responses between 14:22-14:24 UTC during a model update; traffic has been shifted back to stable and we're investigating root cause. No data loss." Waiting Amy signoff. :email:
Amy: message sent to impacted accounts and support queue. One customer asked if we can replay lost requests — engineering: can we surface logs/requests for replay?
Tom: we have request traces with request IDs for that window; we can export sanitized payloads to CS but need approval from privacy/compliance.
Liam: for live mitigation, we should also temporarily enable tighter streaming timeouts and reduce max tokens per chunk to avoid stalls. I'll apply a conservative client-side limit: `streaming.max_chunk_tokens=256` and `streaming.client_timeout_ms=1500`.
Maya: applied those runtime flags to the prod config group for streaming. Monitoring effect.
IncBot: alert cleared for canary-8742 at 3612345799 (SLOs restored).
Elaine: summary for ops board: canary v9.3 caused KV cache thrash leading to tail latency/stalls on streaming. Immediate mitigation: abort canary, shift traffic to stable, tighten streaming chunk/timeouts, notify customers. Next steps: postmortem + mitigation tasks assigned.
Kevin: assigning follow-ups to eng-ml and eng-runtime: I will make a doc with reproducer steps and perf traces.
Maya: handing off to next oncall for the night. @Tom you're next?
Tom: taking handoff. I'll own oncall until 3612349000. Handoff notes: metrics stabilized after abort, keep an eye on p99 < 1s, verify no regressions in bulk-embedding endpoints.
Liam: thanks all. If we need to reattempt rollout, propose gradual shadowing for 24h with KV warmup enabled and no quant path for first 10% traffic.
Amy: CS will follow up with customers tomorrow with post-incident update.
Elaine: closing thread for live mitigation; will link this thread into incident ticket INC-7896 and the eventual postmortem. :white_check_mark:
